result.topic_en: Euler derives the vibration time and sound frequency of an elastic rod, determines the constants α, β, γ, δ from the transcendental condition cos ω = 2/(e^ω + e^{-ω}), and writes the final equation of motion of the rod.
result.transcription:
bimus $f=\frac{a}{\omega}$, hincque $k=\frac{a^4}{bcc\omega^4}$; tum vero erit
$\sqrt{\frac{2g}{k}}=\frac{c\omega\omega\sqrt{2bg}}{aa}$;
quocirca tempus vnius vibrationis erit $=\frac{\pi aa}{\omega\omega c\sqrt{2gb}}$, hincque ipſe ſonus a virga editus $=\frac{\omega\omega c\sqrt{2gb}}{\pi aa}$. Denique cum ſit
$\cos.\,\omega=\frac{2}{e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}}$, erit $\sin.\,\omega=\frac{\pm(e^{\omega}-e^{-\omega})}{e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}}$;
ex priore autem valore, quo ſinus $\omega$ eſt poſitiuus, erit
$\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=\frac{1-e^{-2\omega}-e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}}{-1+e^{2\omega}-e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}}$, hincque
$\frac{\alpha}{\beta}e^{\omega}=\frac{e^{\omega}-e^{-\omega}-e^{2\omega}+1}{-e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}+e^{2\omega}-1}=-1$,
ita vt ſit $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=\frac{-1}{e^{\omega}}=-e^{-\omega}$; altero autem caſu quo ſinus $\omega$ eſt
negatiuus, reperitur $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=+\frac{1}{e^{\omega}}=+e^{-\omega}$; quare ſi ſumamus $\alpha=1$, erit $\beta=\mp e^{\omega}$, hincque $\gamma=1\pm e^{\omega}$ et
$\delta=1\mp e^{\omega}$, vbi ſigna ſuperiora valent, ſi ſin. $\omega$ eſt poſitiuus, inferiora ſi negatiuus. His igitur valoribus inuentis aequatio pro motu virgae perfecte eſt determinata, quae quo ſimplicius repraeſentetur, notetur, ob $f=\frac{a}{\phi}$ eſſe $\frac{s}{f}=\frac{s}{\omega}$;
vnde ſi ponatur breuitatis gratia $\frac{s}{a}=\omega$, vt ſit $\frac{s}{f}=u\,\omega$,
hoc valore poſito aequatio noſtra pro motu erit:
$y=C\sin.(\zeta+t\frac{\omega\omega c\sqrt{2gb}}{aa})(e^{u\omega}\mp e^{\omega(1-u)}+(1\pm e^{\omega})\sin.u\omega+(1\mp e^{\omega})\cos.u\omega)$
ex qua ad quoduis tempus $t$ ſtatus virgae elaſticae cognoſcitur, ſi modo valor literae $\omega$ rite fuerit definitus.

Corol-
